header: 4-robot intersection  ·  take 5 of 5  ·  VLM: Gemini Robotics-ER 2
camera_label: Left: real overhead camera of the simulation (topic /perception/annotated_frame). The boxes and robot ids were drawn on it by the perception module (M1) during the run.
intro_lines: Four robots drive toward a crossing from four sides and jam in the middle. When a robot has been stuck for 12 s, the system asks a vision-language model (VLM) what to do: it sends a text prompt and the current camera image, checks the answer, and executes it.
In this scenario the prompt lists, for each robot, the actions the system's plan verifier would accept. The model picks one action per robot and the order.
Robots: 4  ·  Model: Gemini Robotics-ER 2 (gemini-robotics-er-2-preview)  ·  Take 5 of 5 of this scenario, recorded 2026-11-15. Why this take is shown is stated at the end.
Left: real overhead camera of the simulation. Right: the run's own logs, replayed in sync with simulation time.
watch_for: The model's plan: which robot backs out, yields or crosses, and in which order (yellow lines on the right).
The check: whether the plan is accepted unchanged (orange lines).
On the camera: which robot backs out first.

captions.text: The four robots drive toward the crossing under their normal navigation (Nav2).
Trigger: robot_2 has been stuck for 12 s. The system sends the model a text prompt and the current camera image; the wait for its answer plays in real time.
Model's answer: no congestion yet (strategy=none), so nothing is sent and the robots keep driving.
Trigger: robot_3 has been stuck for 12 s; the four robots are jammed in the middle. The model is asked again.

Model's plan: robot_3 and robot_4 back out (robot_3 first), robot_1 yields, robot_2 crosses. It picked each robot's action from the list of allowed actions in the prompt, and it chose the back-out order.

Check: the plan verifier accepted the plan unchanged (provenance=vlm_verbatim); the back-out order is the model's (dispatch_order_source=model). The system's default order would have put robot_4 first; it was computed offline and is not in these logs.
Dispatch, phase 1: robot_3 is sent 'reverse' (back out); the other three robots are told to wait.
Phase 2: robot_3 has backed out; now robot_4 backs out.
Phase 3: robot_1 yields and robot_2 is escorted across. From here on the order and timing are the system's (the model's crossing_order was not used).

at.match: robot robot_2 arrived at base goal

captions.text: robot_2 has reached its goal; the system now releases the others one at a time.
The model is asked once more while robot_1 is still on its way; it answers 'no congestion', so nothing is sent.

at.match: robot robot_1 arrived at base goal

outcome.text: Outcome: VLM-driven execution: the model's plan and back-out order were executed as written. 4 of 4 robots arrived.

legend: Legend: reverse = back straight out · yield = back out and pull aside · cross = drive through · temporary_wait = hold still · provenance=vlm_verbatim = plan accepted unchanged · dispatch_order_source=model = the back-out order is the model's · 'safety stop … min_distance_violation' (dim) = robots closer than 0.45 m are held still by the safety monitor.
disclosure: Illustrative demo, not controlled experimental evidence.
outro_lines: The model's: each robot's action, chosen from the listed allowed actions, and the back-out order (robot_3 first).

The system's: when to ask; the list of allowed actions; back-out distances; the cross and release phases and everything after the two back-outs. The system's default back-out order was robot_4 first (computed offline). The two orders differ by about 1 cm in the system's cost (a near-tie), so only the timing of the two back-outs changed: robot_3 backed out about 9 s before robot_4.
Why this take: it is the only VLM-driven take of the five. Takes 1–4: one unresolved, three resolved by the grounding module's default plan (M3-default).
